items.label: Mode 50
items.note: A good first recording of the work, which consists of sixteen sonatas and four interludes. Forty-five notes of the piano are prepared, producing a range of small percussion sounds. Vandré plays a small Steinway O with carefully chosen preparations, on an intimate scale; the label’s useful notes explain how the instrument’s string lengths affect the preparations.

items.label: Mode 147
items.note: Cage’s chance operations produced four books of precisely written piano music, made up of sharp attacks, silences and sounds made inside the instrument. The recording is recommended for the sudden attacks and abrupt silences of the score; Joste plays the complicated notation with physical force, and the disc places the work between Seven Haiku and the Suite for Toy Piano.

items.recorded: June 2011, Boutell Memorial Concert Hall, Northern Illinois University, DeKalb
items.label: Mode 243
items.note: Four percussionists play different phrase patterns within the same twenty-four-bar spans, taking turns on tin cans, rattles, drums and a conch shell. Third Coast’s recording has rhythmic drive and clearly separated instruments, and couples the piece with the other two Constructions; Gregory Beyer and Ross Karre play in First Construction. The filmed edition shows the players moving rapidly between instruments.

items.performers: Essential Music; John Kennedy and Charles Wood, directors
items.label: Mode 239
items.note: Essential Music plays Five by blowing into bottles, which take the sustained pitches, an instrumental choice Cage approved. Seven and Thirteen expand the group. These late works allow players to place their sounds within specified time-brackets, and sustained notes overlap without a conductor coordinating their entries.
